title: Volume 1 - Chapter 6: The Quality of Magic Power
content: Chapter 6: The Quality of Magic Power
To put it bluntly, the experiment ended in failure.
The development team was adjusting the machine and trying to draw out my magic power, but the fundamental problem lay with me, the test pilot.
A significant lack of magic power output.
With my magic power far below the required threshold, I couldn't withstand combat against Gijuu.
No matter how much they enhanced the machine or the Magic Power Converter, it was meaningless if the crucial magic power output was completely insufficient.
At present, my priority should be to increase my magic power output.
However, the development team had little know-how regarding magic.
"I want advice on how to improve my magic power output, huh?"
That night, after the experiment, I visited Dr. Alison's office.
The small room, separated only by partitions in the hangar, was neatly arranged with Dr. Alison's PC and stacks of documents and books.
Most of it was work-related, but there was a single picture frame sitting on the desk.
"I understand your desire to seek advice, but you know we have little know-how ourselves, right?"
"I decided to rely on the doctors who have more knowledge than I do."
"Did you ask Dr. Smith?"
"He said that increasing the ratio of Gijuu cells would be the quickest way. At the same time, he mentioned that even if I replaced my entire body, I wouldn't reach the expected figures."
"…Hah, that guy really is something."
As Dr. Alison let out a deep sigh, she offered me her advice.
"I'm sorry, but we have too little know-how regarding magic to make any predictions. By the way, do you have any solutions in mind?"
"I'm considering increasing my training time and switching to a more intense regimen to better integrate my limbs. …This is all I can do right now."
The reason I couldn't meet the required output was that I wasn't fully utilizing the magic power from the Gijuu cells.
I thought of increasing my training as a way to better integrate my limbs.
I didn't expect to solve the problem with my own method.
That's why I turned to the doctors for help.
Dr. Alison smiled wryly.
"If that would solve it, we would have resolved it a long time ago. Alright, let me give you some advice."
Seeing me sit up straight and listen earnestly, Dr. Alison chuckled.
"It's not a big deal. If we lack the know-how, we can draw from those who do."
"Those who have it, you say?"
Should I access a specialized institution? However, I couldn't imagine that I would be able to investigate that with my current authority.
Dr. Alison looked at my confusion with exasperation.
"Looking back, we should be grateful for the principal's whim. …You're enrolled in a class with Valkyries who excel in handling magic, right?"
With that said, she shot me a look that seemed to say, "You understand now, right?" Grasping the hint, I saluted her.
"Thank you for your advice!"
I almost forgot in the atmosphere of the academy, but they were Valkyries, the main players on the battlefield.
They were the ones most skilled in handling magic and possessed the know-how.
Dr. Alison stood up and placed her hand on my shoulder.
"Make sure to extract the information well. Just be careful not to raise suspicion from the principal or those around you."
"Understood! I will do my utmost!"
I was determined to acquire the know-how regarding magic for the sake of Dr. Alison and the development team.
However, Dr. Alison wore a worried expression.
"…Are you really going to be okay?"
To acquire the know-how regarding magic, I attended Class Five at the academy.
I was attending the class more earnestly than usual, hoping to glean some hints, but it seemed that Louise noticed something off about me.
As soon as the break started, she approached me.
"Ren-kun, you're especially serious today. Is something up?"
Louise didn't seem to be probing me; she genuinely appeared to be concerned.
"…I want to improve my magic power output, and I thought there might be hints in the lessons."
"Ah, I see. But that might be a bit difficult?"
I asked Louise why she thought so, noticing her troubled expression.
"Why is that?"
I desperately tried to maintain my composure, not wanting her to sense my urgency.
Louise looked up and began to share her understanding of Valkyries' perception of magic.
"Classes related to magic are conducted in the middle school. By the time everyone graduates, they meet a certain standard. In high school, the curriculum prioritizes other subjects."
"I-I see."
It seemed unlikely that I would gain any know-how regarding magic from the classes.
Then, it appeared I had no choice but to ask someone.
As the next class was about to start, I tried to end the conversation, but Louise seemed eager to continue.
"Could it be that you're having issues related to magic?"
"…I can't discuss that."
"Oh, I see. It's military confidential, huh? Then you can't say anything."
Nodding along, Louise then made a suggestion.
"Then I'll teach you about magic. It's the basics that even middle schoolers know, but still."
"Is that alright?"
Looking at Louise, who was unexpectedly cheerful, she wore a broad smile.
"Of course! We're friends, right? If you're in trouble, we should help each other out."
"Friends… you say."
Seeing my reaction, Louise tilted her head.
"What's wrong? Is it that you don't want to be friends with me?"
"No, that's not it. I've spent so long in military life that I have very few people I can call friends."
"Is that so? Did you not get along with the people in your previous unit?"
I recalled the squad that had been wiped out before I arrived here.
My relationship with them hadn't been bad; in fact, it had been quite good.
However, infantry units are prone to heavy attrition.
Making friends requires a certain level of resolve.
"…They were comrades. Besides, I was taught that it's not desirable to form relationships beyond comrades on the battlefield."
I had been told to avoid getting too close to anyone, as it could cloud my judgment in battle.
For some reason, I found myself clenching my hands tightly.
Noticing my behavior, Louise smiled sadly.
"I see. Infantry life is tough, huh? I'm sorry for asking something strange."
"It's fine. More importantly, will you really teach me?"
Louise lightly thumped her large chest with her fist.
"Leave it to me! Despite how I look, I've been told I'm good at taking care of others!"
Her words, directed at someone like me who was an oddity at the academy, carried a certain persuasive power.
After school.
I was learning about magic from Louise.
We were in the academy's library, and despite it being after school, there were a fair number of female students using the space.
"Magic is closely tied to the heart."
"The heart, you say? Is that about mental strength?"
"Well, that is important too, I guess? But the most important thing is motivation, I think? For us, it's the feeling of wanting to become Valkyries and fight against Gijuu!"
"So it's a matter of feelings?"
This left me somewhat perplexed.
I had been fighting against Gijuu for years.
It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say that I had lived to fight.
"I've been fighting Gijuu since I was an infantryman."
"That's just fighting. What's important is whether your own will is there."
"…Will."
Since losing my family, I had been living as I was told.
I was picked up by an organization and followed the orders of the adults in the training facility.
Once thrown into the battlefield, I fought against Gijuu under the command of my superiors.
What I realized from Louise's words was the fact that I had lacked my own will in all of that.
"No, from now on, I will fight with my own will."
If simply wanting to fight against Gijuu was enough, then it was indeed a matter of mentality.
I felt a glimmer of hope, but Louise's expression was clouded.

"It's not just about vaguely believing that. It's about having a strong desire from the bottom of your heart, I think? It's not something you do because someone told you to; it needs to be a self-driven motivation. That… with how you are now, I think it might be difficult."
"Is that so!? …No, I apologize."
As I raised my voice in the quiet library, I drew the attention of the surrounding female students, who looked at me with reproach.
Some of them seemed curious about what was going on, but as I lowered my voice, they seemed to lose interest.
Louise urged me to calm down.

"I understand how you feel, but this is a matter that relates to one's innate quality. Back in middle school, there were plenty of kids who were better than me in terms of grades. But most of them ended up dropping out because they couldn't draw out their magic power well."
That was a stark contrast to my childhood.
In the facility, grades were everything.
No matter how motivated you were, if your grades were low, you were deemed unfit and would disappear from the facility before you knew it.
"Then what should I do…?"
At this rate, I wouldn't meet the required magic power output.
That would mean the loss of my very existence.
Surely my expression was dark.
Louise clasped her hands together and offered me comfort.
"Don't be down, Ren-kun. Um… oh!"
Standing up, Louise began searching the library's bookshelf for something.
She quickly returned with a book in hand.
The title was something along the lines of "How to Be Positive."

"This is perfect for you, who tends to get down! It's a great solution that will help you become more positive and improve your magic control. If you read this, you'll definitely be able to handle magic!"
I couldn't deny that my personality wasn't exactly bright, nor could I say I was optimistic.
Receiving the book from Louise, I asked, "Will reading this really solve my problems?"
"Yep! I'm sure it will improve your magic control. So cheer up!"
Though the words she used seemed slightly off, I convinced myself that the differences in perception regarding magic between the academy and the development team were to blame.
I flipped through the book and then closed it.
"Thank you. I'll read it as soon as I get home."
As I expressed my gratitude, I noticed Louise blushing and scratching her cheek with her fingertip.
"Don't worry about it. We're… friends, after all."
"Y-yes."
Being called a friend filled me with an odd mix of embarrassment and happiness.
Is this what youth feels like? I wondered.
As time flowed by, which had been foreign to me, a loud footstep echoed in the library as a female student approached us.
No one among the surrounding girls reprimanded the noisy student.
When I turned to face her, I found myself looking at the stern-faced Lieutenant Hayase.
"I didn't think you'd still be doing this. Louise, you really are persistent."
Lieutenant Hayase's gaze was directed at Louise.
She had come to reprimand Louise for defending me, who was disliked at the academy.
Louise, looking down, resisted.
"What I do is my own business, Hayase-san. I'm acting because I want to help Ren-kun. I would appreciate it if you didn't interfere… maybe."
For Louise, Lieutenant Hayase was also a superior, and while I didn't know the details, she was likely of a higher rank in the academy's rules, which didn't emphasize military discipline.
To protect Louise's position, I stood up and stepped in front of Lieutenant Hayase.
"Lieutenant Hayase, this was my request. If you must blame someone, please blame me."
The look Lieutenant Hayase gave me was filled with disdain.
It was the same look that soldiers had given me at various bases, seeing me as an oddity.
With Gijuu cells within me, I was viewed as filth… no, as an enemy.
"It seems you've managed to tame him quite well. But really, you… huh?"
Lieutenant Hayase's gaze shifted to the book I was holding under my arm.
Then it turned to Louise.
"I don't know what your intentions are, but if you continue to do as you please, be prepared for the consequences."
As a tense atmosphere began to surround Lieutenant Hayase, the female students in the library started to flee.
Instead of energetic female students, a woman in a slit lady's suit entered.
For a moment, I mistook her for a student because of the aura she exuded.
With her long brown hair tied up, she pointed at Lieutenant Hayase as soon as she entered the library.
"Ah! Maya-chan is bullying students from other classes! That's not acceptable! As a teacher, I won't allow it!"
Though she seemed angry, her demeanor was lighthearted.
She was merely pouting in a way that didn't seem scary at all.
However, it seemed to have an effect on Lieutenant Hayase.
Letting out a deep sigh, she turned her back to us.
"Minami-sensei, could you please refrain from making such a loud statement that sounds bad? I was just trying to help."
[img]https://i.imgur.com/szKVlDu.jpeg
Hearing Lieutenant Hayase's claim of trying to help, Louise muttered under her breath.
"…That's a bit disingenuous, Hayase-san."
Fortunately, it seemed that the other party didn't hear her, which was a relief, but there seemed to be something deep-rooted between the two.
The person who had come to the library was Minami-sensei… apparently a teacher.
"Don't make excuses! Maya-chan is the ace of Class Three! So you need to be careful about your behavior. I hate bullying, so I won't allow it."
The first impression I had of Class Three's teacher was that she was a childish person, just as she looked.
Lieutenant Hayase seemed to be weak against Minami-sensei, scratching her head with a troubled expression.
"You say that, but what do you want?"
"Oh, right! We're having a briefing soon, so gather in the conference room! Maya-chan, you need to come with me."
"Why not just call me on the terminal?"
"That's not it! When I tried to call, there was a commotion, so I rushed over and found Maya-chan here!"
"Yes, yes."
Lieutenant Hayase spoke casually to the teacher, who seemed to be her superior, which was unbelievable to me.
However, Minami-sensei didn't seem to mind.
Speaking disrespectfully to a superior was unthinkable for me.
The privileges of being an ace… remembering Louise's words, I realized that the academy was a different organization from the military.
As the two of them left the library, the remaining female students sighed in relief as if a storm had passed.
Louise stood up.
"Ren-kun, can I talk to you for a moment?"
Though we had planned to disperse in the library, I followed Louise's invitation, and we headed to the rooftop.
Once we arrived on the rooftop, Louise turned her back to me, clasped her hands together, and stretched.
The wind threatened to lift her skirt, so I stepped in front of her to block the view and placed my hands on the safety railing.
"Did something happen with Lieutenant Hayase?"
Louise smiled wryly as she began to speak about her relationship with Lieutenant Hayase.
"…I'm not liked. Hayase-san seems to have a strong desire to rise in rank, I guess? So, she seems to dislike laid-back girls like me."
Recalling Lieutenant Hayase's behavior, I could indeed see her strong-willed side.
I had seen many prideful and ambitious soldiers before, and it felt like Lieutenant Hayase shared some of those traits. …I felt that way, but whether they were the same or not was a different matter.
There might be differences due to the military and the academy, but I couldn't come to a conclusion.
It seemed that kind-hearted Louise simply didn't mesh well with her.
It appeared that aces were granted privileges, but seeing the other female students shrink back in fear made it seem excessive.
When Louise came to my side, she grasped the railing and hung her head.
"I was scouted by Class Three once. The interview went well, but in the end, Hayase-san didn't want me, so the transfer talk fell through."
"Is that allowed?"
To be deemed unfit based on a single person's opinion… that was strange to me.
"That's the privilege of being an ace. Well, it's common practice to listen to the opinions of the class when it comes to transfers, but it's rare for it to be so blatant… I think?"
Having been in Class Five, I had come to understand something.
The female students aimed to transfer to Classes One through Four, which were recognized as the elite Valkyries.
If they were transferred, they would be deployed to actual combat, but they would also be treated preferentially.
It seemed that there was more to it than just the treatment, but for those who graduated from middle school, they were considered elite.
For the ambitious female students, getting transferred seemed to carry more significance than just a promotion.
"If it's Louise, you'll get scouted by other classes."
"Ahaha, thanks, Ren-kun. I'm happy even if it's just comforting words. But you see, being scouted by Class Three means they are currently lacking in strength."
"What do you mean by that?"

"About three years ago, Class Three's unit was wiped out. Right now, they're in the process of rebuilding. To the kids in Class Five, the truth is that they'd rather join another class than Class Three."
In other words, being scouted by Class Three and not being allowed to transfer was equivalent to receiving a notice of being unfit for Louise.
"Well, in a way… it was my last hope. But Hayase-san crushed it, so now I have no chances left."
Seeing her smile bitterly in resignation, I naturally recalled certain words.
My mother's words from long ago.
"…Move forward, step by step."
"Huh?"
Louise looked extremely surprised by my sudden muttering.
Her expression, which I had never seen before, made her look like a different person for a moment.
With wide eyes, she turned her face away from me, looking out beyond the railing.
It seemed I had made another mistake.
"I apologize. I just remembered something my mother used to say."
"I-I see. You surprised me when you suddenly said that. …By the way, who did you hear it from?"

"My mother. She said it meant to move forward step by step without being swayed by those around you. So, Louise, you should also focus on the efforts you can make without worrying about others' evaluations… no, that wasn't advice I should be giving you right now."
Though I had spoken the words I remembered, they applied more to me than to Louise.
For me, who had lost my sense of purpose, the only thing I could do was to build up what I could do now.
"That's a good saying. Yes, it's really a good saying. It makes me want to try harder too."
Though her voice lacked energy, and she seemed down, Louise was forcing a smile as she looked at me.
"Thank you, Ren-kun. Well then, I'll take my leave now. Starting tomorrow, Hayase-san's interference will probably continue, but let's work together to get through it!"
"Yes."
Then, as if she remembered something, Louise added, "Oh, and tomorrow is an important class for you, so make sure to attend."
"I don't think there are any classes that aren't important."
At my response, Louise smiled awkwardly, but then her expression turned mischievous as she said, "It's a class related to magic. And it might be a fun class for you, Ren-kun, being a boy."
"Ah, I see. I was already planning to attend, so unless there's an emergency, I will definitely be there."
Hearing my answer, Louise blushed and smiled.
"Make sure to attend!"
Though I was the pilot of the experimental machine, I was also a student in Class Five at the academy.
Naturally, I was obligated to participate in the training included in the curriculum.
As a pilot of the experimental machine, a meticulous training regimen was prepared for me.
Therefore, I honestly wanted to avoid unnecessary training as much as possible, but since I was enrolled in Class Five, it was unthinkable to not participate.
I was personally interested in what kind of training the Valkyrie candidates were undergoing.
However, I regretted that I should have skipped this particular training.
"Alright, let's start with warm-ups. One, two, one, two…"
A female student stood in front of her classmates, performing stretching exercises in the academy-designated swimsuit.
The students in Class Five were following along, stretching their bodies in the same manner.
The girls were wearing high-cut competitive swimsuits, or so I was told by Louise, who was shyly stretching next to me.
I had little experience using a pool outside of training, so I had no knowledge of women's swimsuits whatsoever.
Every time Louise moved her body, her chest swayed, and her rear was accentuated, making it difficult for me to know where to look.
Even if I turned my gaze elsewhere, all I could see were female students doing their warm-ups.
As I struggled to find a place to focus my eyes, I noticed that Louise was blushing and smiling shyly.

"Honestly, I didn't expect to be in a pool with boys. The swimsuits are chosen for ease of movement, so isn't this the best environment for boys? …B-but, even though I invited you, I feel a bit embarrassed right now."
As Louise looked around, it seemed that the atmosphere was different from usual.
Perhaps because I was there, many of the girls doing their warm-ups were also feeling shy.
I felt an unusual amount of attention directed at me.
The swimsuit provided for me was said to be a half-spats type, covering up to just above the knee.
As I was stretching like the girls, I could hear whispers around me.
Though I couldn't catch what they were saying, it felt wrong for me to be in this situation.
The instructor, who had also changed into a swimsuit, approached us, wearing a whistle around her neck, and blew it sharply, producing a loud sound.
Gathering everyone's attention, she turned to the girls while looking at me.
"Don't hold back just because there's a boy here."
The instructor, sounding annoyed, warned the students, and I raised my hand to seek permission to speak.
She let out a small sigh.
"What is it, Ichinose?"
"Yes, Instructor. I believe I am not suited for this situation. I would like to request a different training regimen."
It was inappropriate for me to participate in a swimming class surrounded by female students.
When I asked for a different training menu, the instructor frowned, looking displeased.
"Are you asking us to prepare a separate menu just for you? Don't get ahead of yourself. Since you've been assigned to Class Five, you must follow Class Five's rules."
"B-but, in this situation, it might cause trouble for those around me."
"That's not for you to decide. Get back to your warm-ups."
"…I apologize."
As I returned to my warm-ups, Louise, who had been standing tall next to me, smiled at me.
"What's wrong? Are you perhaps bad at swimming, Ren-kun?"
"No, I can swim just fine. When I was an infantryman, I even trained swimming while fully clothed."
I had been made to swim while wearing not just clothes but also equipment.
I had been splashed with water by instructors and had nearly drowned countless times.
As Louise bent forward, she began to talk to me about the importance of swimming.
"You should definitely participate in swimming class. There are exceptions, but kids who are good at magic control tend to do well in swimming classes."
I was surprised by the information Louise shared regarding magic control.
I had never thought that magic and swimming were related.
"Is that so? So that's why you told me to make sure to attend yesterday."
It seemed to be a common understanding for Louise, and she spoke of it as if it weren't that important.
"That's right. The feeling of being in the water seems somewhat similar to magic control. That's why kids who are good at magic control tend to swim a lot."
"Thank you for sharing such important information."
As I expressed my gratitude, Louise smiled wryly.
"You really are serious, Ren-kun. That's one of your good points, I guess."
Once the warm-ups ended, my body had loosened up and warmed up.
I thought I would be able to focus on the swimming class without any issues, but I once again felt the gaze of the surrounding female students on my body.
"Look at that scar."
"More than the scar, look at his limbs. The regenerated areas are a different color, right?"
"How awful to be in the pool with a monster."
For the female students, being in the pool with me, who had Gijuu limbs, likely evoked a strong sense of aversion.
As I pretended not to hear, Louise placed her palm against my left arm.
She began to pat my body gently.
"…What are you doing, Louise?"
"Ahaha. I was just thinking you have an amazing body. After all, men have such impressive muscles. And you're covered in scars… does it hurt?"
If you participated in battles against Gijuu, you would inevitably get hurt.
My body was covered in scars, but my regenerated right arm and left leg were pristine without a single mark.
"All of them are old scars, so they don't hurt now."
"I see. That's good, then."
Louise smiled at me, seemingly worried that I might be hurt by the heartless voices around us.
When the instructor blew the whistle sharply, she turned to us with an irritated expression.
"Hey, how long are you going to play around? Get your bodies used to the water and get into the pool."
After finishing her statement, the instructor turned her back to us and began to admonish the other excited female students.
Louise watched this and chuckled, leaving me wondering what was so funny.
"What's so amusing?"
"The instructor is also conscious of you, Ren-kun, and that's why it's funny."
"The instructor? I didn't see that at all."
She was still admonishing the excited female students and didn't seem to be paying attention to me.
However, it seemed that Louise, who had been around longer, saw things differently.
"Isn't it strange that she seems more energetic than usual? Since it was all girls until now, it's not surprising that the instructor would be conscious of you."
"Is that how it works?"
As I remained unconvinced, Louise grabbed my left hand and pulled me.
"Come on, let's hurry and get into the pool. The first ten minutes are free time, so we can play around!"
It seemed we were allowed to play for the first ten minutes to get used to the water.
This was a stark contrast to the training I had undergone.
"Understood, but please don't pull so hard, Louise. Louise? Wait, Louise!? First, we need to get our bodies wet—"
Ignoring my words, Louise pulled me along and dashed toward the pool.
With her left arm wrapped around mine, her chest pressed against me.
"Louise, um, your chest—"
Disregarding my words, Louise maintained her momentum and jumped into the pool.
"Here we go!"
As we both splashed into the water, the instructor blew her whistle loudly.
"Louise, and Ichinose! Get back here!"
The pool was indoors and equipped with diving boards, with depths exceeding five meters.
It seemed that a generous budget had been allocated for the facilities to train Valkyries.
Once we finished getting used to the water, the training finally began.
Everyone swam fifty meters in a crawl, and when they finished, they got out of the water and returned to the starting position.
After returning, they would jump back into the pool and repeat the act of swimming.
The female students who had been frolicking just a moment ago now wore serious expressions.
The instructor held a tablet in one arm, alternating her gaze between the students and the screen.
"Your pace is slowing down. If you can't take training seriously, don't expect to perform well in actual combat. Those who try to hold back will find their evaluations dropping rapidly."
As if reacting to the instructor's words about evaluations, the movements of the female students changed.
The girls swimming picked up their pace, and those returning to the starting position began to run.
As I got out of the pool and returned to the starting position, I noticed that Louise, who had already gotten out of the water, offered me her hand.
Using her wet hand, I climbed out of the pool.
"Everyone seems to be taking this more seriously now."
"When evaluations are mentioned, we have no choice but to do our best. Come on, Ren-kun, hurry up!"
As Louise urged me, I rushed back to the starting position, noticing that many of the girls were showing signs of fatigue.
However, among them, there were also girls who showed no signs of tiredness.
All the students in Class Five were candidates who had successfully graduated from middle school.
They were generally excellent and recognized as capable of becoming regular members at any time.
Even among them, the differences in ability were clearly evident.
As I waited for my turn to dive at the starting position, Louise, who was lined up in the adjacent lane, spoke to me.
“Ren-kun, don’t you think you’re looking at the other girls too much when I’m right here? It’s terrible~ I’m getting jealous~”
Though she said she was jealous, Louise was smiling mischievously like a playful child.
It seemed she was enjoying teasing me.
“That’s not it. I was just curious.”
“Curious about what?”
“To be honest, I was surprised. Everyone in Class Five has great stamina.”
The swimming class used up two periods, making it longer than usual.
There was time set aside for play at the beginning, but after that, we were made to swim at a fast pace the entire time.
Even I, who had been training until now, was starting to feel out of breath, while many of the girls weren’t showing any signs of fatigue at all.
Louise was one of them.
“Well, we’re still candidates. If we’re out of breath at this level, we won’t even make it to high school.”
Louise said this as if it were the most obvious thing in the world, and she looked quite relaxed in my eyes.
“You stand out among them, Louise.”
“Huh? Are you trying to flirt with me? What a sinful woman I am~!”
Louise was being playful, but our turn was coming up, so the conversation ended there.
After swimming and a lunch break in the afternoon.
All the students in Class Five had changed into their gym uniforms and gathered in the gymnasium.
“I have good news for you tired swimmers. To keep you from dozing off during the theory class, we’re going to have a practical training session instead.”
When the instructor explained that we would be doing practical training, the girls made faces that clearly showed their displeasure.
I wondered if it was okay for them to be so negative, and Louise, who was firmly keeping her position to my left, answered my unspoken question.
“Practical training isn’t effective against Gijuu, so everyone’s not motivated.”
“I see. However, won’t making a face in front of the instructor lower your evaluation?”
“If you’re good at practical training, you get evaluated in a different way, so many girls have mixed feelings about it.”
“Is there something wrong with that?”
“...Even those who graduate without becoming regular members can get jobs in public safety-related departments if they have excellent practical training scores.”
I had heard that there were units that dealt with humans instead of Gijuu, but it seemed from Louise’s tone that being recognized in that way wasn’t something to be happy about.
“Isn’t that a bad thing?”
“For us who want to become regular members, it’s a job we can get after graduating without any results. Riding a battle dress is appealing, but facing humans is a bit different.”
It seemed that for them, who had trained to defeat Gijuu, it was something they couldn’t fully accept.
Before I knew it, the instructor’s explanation had ended, and training was about to start in pairs.
As Louise turned to face me, she readied a rubber knife.
“Well then, Ren-kun, let’s train together. Don’t worry. Despite how I look, I’ve trained a bit, so you won’t get hurt even if I’m your opponent—”
But before Louise could finish, another girl stepped in front of me, pushing her aside.
With short hair and a well-toned body, she had tanned brown skin.
“Louise, sorry, but can you step aside? I need to teach this former infantryman not to get too cocky.”
Louise looked slightly annoyed at the girl who had cut in and warned her.
“Hey, don’t just cut in like that!”
“Just let me have my turn. Or are you too scared to fight unless it’s against Louise?”
The girl brandished her rubber knife, but she didn’t seem like a seasoned fighter.
I thought it was a cheap provocation, but I quietly readied my knife with my left hand.
Louise looked a bit surprised at my stance.
Since I was usually right-handed in Class Five, holding the knife with my left hand must have made it look like I was slacking off.

The reason I was using my left hand was that it was more reliable in combat than my right hand after rehabilitation, but the girl standing in front of me seemed to have misinterpreted it as me looking down on her.
“Don’t mess with me! Just because you’re a former infantryman, don’t think you can look down on us!”
The girl took a big step forward... and the next moment, she was trying to dive into my space.
There was more than two meters between us, yet she closed the distance in an instant.
I quickly deflected the knife she swung at me.
The first thing I felt was her incredible speed.
It wasn’t a refined movement typical of a seasoned fighter; it was just a raw display of physical ability.
The girl laughed as she saw my eyes widen in surprise.
“Don’t compare our physical abilities to those of ordinary humans!”
She seemed confident in her physical prowess, which wasn’t surprising.
She certainly had a well-trained physique, but to me, the girls in Class Five looked slender.
Compared to the strong soldiers I had been surrounded by when I was an infantryman, they seemed to have less muscle mass.
However, their movements surpassed those of trained soldiers.
I recalled the battles with the attackers.
I dodged the knife the girl thrust at me, but it grazed my cheek.
“Fast!”
While watching her movements, I made the minimum necessary movements to evade and blocked her attack with the knife in my left hand.
As I focused on evading and observing, I could sense the girl’s growing frustration.
Her movements were becoming increasingly reckless.
“Do you think you can win just by running away? Come at me a little!”
I could feel her anger rising, and I kept my eyes on her quick movements.
I knew she wasn’t putting much emphasis on practical training, but there was more waste in her movements than I had imagined.
Using her overwhelming physical abilities to try to dominate was her fighting style.
“What’s the matter? Want to use some Gijuu power?”
She seemed to be trying to provoke me into using the power of Gijuu.
She probably wanted to overwhelm me after making me use it.
“I don’t need it.”
When I refused, her face clearly showed her irritation.
“You mean you don’t need it because you think you’re better than me!”
No, she was probably underestimating me, thinking I was inferior.
The girl swung her knife and incorporated a kick into her attack.
Her impatience to win, stemming from her inability to land a hit, was evident.
“Why can’t I hit you?!”
If she had fought calmly from the start, she might have had a chance to win.
As she carelessly stepped in, I took a step forward as well, grabbing her arm to stop her momentum.
Realizing she had made a mistake, I threw her off balance and applied a joint lock.
No matter how strong they were, their joints were still human.
As I pinned her to the floor, the girl struggled desperately for several seconds before finally giving in and relaxing her body.
“...I give up.”
“Thank you very much.”
As I released the joint lock and stepped back cautiously, the girl pounded the floor in frustration.
From my perspective, the girl I had fought was lacking compared to the attackers.
The attackers, especially the leader among them, had been superior in hand-to-hand combat.
I had heard that the attackers were likely former Valkyries, but if they were receiving regular training, that would be a troubling situation.
The possibility of them operating as an organized group had just increased.
Other girls gathered around the girl I had defeated.
“What are you doing?”
“It’s impossible to lose to an ordinary guy!”
The girl, being scolded by those around her, shouted in anger from her frustration.
“Shut up! I wasn’t even trying hard in practical training!”
I turned my gaze away from the girl making excuses, and before I knew it, Louise was by my side.
She was peering up at my face.
“What’s up?”
“You were amazing, Ren-kun! I didn’t think you could win so easily against that girl, even though her close combat scores weren’t bad!”
Louise looked genuinely surprised, her expression serious this time.
“I’ve been training too, you know.”
I was surprised that the earlier girl was receiving high praise.
It seemed that the academy didn’t place much emphasis on practical combat.

“We’re the same in that regard. Besides, even if we have better physical abilities, I didn’t expect you to win so easily. You were able to fight back when we were attacked too... Do you have some kind of secret?”
“There's no secret at all.”
When I remained silent, for some reason, Louise wouldn’t let it go.
This time, she kept throwing the same question at me, as if she wouldn’t let me escape.
“Did you undergo some special training? Or do the infantry have some special treatment? I think there must be some secret behind those movements!”
Feeling cornered by Louise, I turned to look at the girl I had fought.
She still seemed unable to accept what had happened, but there was a reason I had won.
While the time difference in training for practical combat might have played a role, the main reason was the environment.
“There really isn’t any special secret. Just—”
“Just?”
“—the opponents I fought on the battlefield were always Gijuu that were stronger than humans. Half-hearted martial arts wouldn’t work against Gijuu.”
From my perspective, having survived that hellish battlefield, the opponents I faced were always stronger beings than humans.
The reason I could win against the girls in Class Five was simply that it was easier than fighting Gijuu.
“If she had been more skilled, the outcome would have been different.”
If she had taken practical training more seriously, I would likely have lost by now.
Their physical specs were that impressive.
However, it seemed Louise didn’t think so.
“I don’t think it’s just a simple difference in skill. I think you have talent, Ren-kun, for being able to win calmly in that situation. It’s probably an amazing talent.”
Talent, huh.
I might have been more fortunate in talent than other soldiers, but even so, I was still at a level where I couldn’t do anything against the suddenly appearing Gijuu.
“My talent is nothing special.”
As I clenched my right hand tightly, wishing I were stronger, for some reason, Louise’s eyes widened in surprise.
I was curious about her reaction and asked her.
“Is something wrong?”
“N-Nothing! So, how about training with me next? Now that I know you’re strong, I won’t hold back!”
Louise showed me her stance with the knife, but I felt she was less skilled than the previous girl.
“Alright, Ren-kun, get ready.”
“Uh, well... okay. Let’s get started then.”
